newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling steady against dollar on exports.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling steady against dollar on exports.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling on Friday held steady against the dollar, supported by coffee and tea exporters selling dollars, commercial bank dealers said on Friday.
Commercial banks said the shilling was trading at a mean rate of 69.8 against the dollar at noon from 69.97 at the open on Friday.
Dealers said sentiment for the shilling, which was bearish after the International Monetary Fund halted a $205 million aid package on July 31, appeared to be changing.
The IMF decision jolted Kenya's currency and equity markets and panicked foreign investors who rushed into the market buying dollars and eroding East Africa's strongest currrency.
The shilling's total losses stand at 17.3 percent since July 31.
Market analysts said higher interest rates offered by the central bank to finance government borrowing could reverse the shilling's misfortunes if foreign investors came back seeking treasury bills.
"People are hesitant to take positions above 70 because they could get burnt if the market receives a flood of dollars from investors in treasury bills," a senior dealer said.
Average yields offered on the benchmark 91-day treasury bills went up at the weekly central bank auction on Thursday to 18.783 percent from 18.199 percent last week.
